title: FlyHash for LLM Agent Memory: An Empirical Validation and a New Application
abstract: arXiv:2611.05791v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on external memory stores to retain information across conversations, typically via dense vector embeddings searched with approximate nearest-neighbor methods. The fruit fly's olfactory circuit computes a locality-sensitive hash of sensory input using a strikingly different mechanism - sparse random projection followed by winner-take-all competition - and prior work (Dasgupta et al., 2017) showed this scheme, dubbed FlyHash, preserves neighbor structure better per bit than conventional random-hyperplane hashing (SimHash) on several benchmarks. translated_title: 面向大语言模型智能体记忆的FlyHash：实证验证与新应用
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）智能体日益依赖外部记忆库来在对话之间保留信息，通常通过稠密向量嵌入并结合近似最近邻搜索方法实现。果蝇的嗅觉回路以一种截然不同的机制计算感觉输入的局部敏感哈希——先进行稀疏随机投影，再进行胜者通吃竞争——先前的研究表明，这种被称为FlyHash的方案在多个基准测试上，每比特的邻居结构保持能力优于传统的随机超平面哈希。据我们所知，本文首次将FlyHash应用于LLM智能体记忆检索，并提出了三个实践者真正需要回答的问题：在正确匹配位数的协议下，质量优势是否依然成立（答案是肯定的，在10个随机种子和涵盖两种模态的四个数据集上均稳健成立，并揭示了一个此前未被记录的具体比较结果……
tldr: 本文首次将受果蝇嗅觉回路启发的FlyHash稀疏哈希应用于大语言模型智能体的记忆检索，并通过严谨的匹配位协议实验实证验证了其相比SimHash的稳健质量优势。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first application of FlyHash, a sparse hashing scheme inspired by the fruit fly olfactory circuit, to LLM agent memory retrieval, empirically validating its robust quality advantage over SimHash under a correctly matched-bit protocol.
